text:
River,

November. From 'novem,' nine. It was the ninth month once, back when the Roman year started in March and the world made marginally more sense. Then someone decided January should go first, February got involved, and now we're stuck with a month called Nine sitting in the eleventh slot — like a guest who arrived at the wrong party and committed fully.

I was cataloguing this at 2am because sleep is a concept I aspire to more than practise. The other thing I catalogue at 2am is the exact colour your eyes go in low light. Somewhere between copper and conspiracy. Less historically rigorous. Significantly more rewarding.

I love you. Even in the eleventh month, when it should be the ninth.

Gale
